question: What water environments does the St. Lawrence system include, and why is calling the entire system either a freshwater river or an ocean too simple?

But the St. Lawrence also includes a number of marine environments, such as estuaries, salt marshes and coastal waters. It all depends on the location where you are along the St. Lawrence system. The St. Lawrence estuary, which is located between the city of Québec and the Saguenay Fjord, is where the fresh and salt waters mix. This is also the case in the Upper Estuary, which is located between Pointe-aux-Trembles and Saint-Zotique. The estuaries and salt marshes are home to a rich diversity of life. The salinity level of the waters in these environments varies, depending on the location and the time of year. These variations create very specific and interesting ecosystems. These wetlands are home to a large number of species of plants and animals, including the copper redhorse, a fish that is found only in Canada and is at risk of extinction. It is important to protect these environments so that we can continue to enjoy all that the St. Lawrence has to offer!
